paragraphs: Skyscanner is a website and app where people search for flights and hotels and compare prices. India is now its biggest market, according to the travel news site Skift. Searches from India rose 22% from a year earlier. Around the world, Skyscanner's searches grew 17%, so India is growing faster than the average.

More Indians are also going overseas. Skyscanner sends its users to airline and travel websites to book. Three years ago, about 80% of these bookings from India were for trips inside the country, and just 20% were international. Today, the split is almost even: 52% domestic and 48% international. The change took three years, and it is large.

Neel Ghose, a travel trends expert at Skyscanner India, spoke to journalists in Delhi about the company's new report, Travel Trends 2027. The report examines what Indian travelers want next year and gives insight into their plans. It is based on a survey of 2,000 Indian travelers that Skyscanner had done in July 2026.

The survey highlights a strong interest in travel abroad. According to the report, 58% of Indians plan to travel abroad more in 2027. Also, 56% plan to spend more on flights, and 44% plan to spend more on places to stay.

Value is an important consideration. Skift reports that Indian travelers book about 28 days before a trip. That is about half the time seen in several other major markets. Their trips are also short, about 3.1 days on average. In the survey, 67% said they had changed a holiday destination, or thought about it, because another place offered better value. So affordable choices matter to many travelers.

The report also highlights technology. In the survey, 87% of Indians said they are confident using artificial intelligence, or AI, to plan and book travel. More than half plan to use artificial intelligence to research destinations. However, accuracy remains a key consideration for more than half of travelers. They want answers that are reliable. Skyscanner also told Skift that, because of concerns about accuracy, it has no clear sign yet that travelers often let AI finish a booking for them. For now, AI is a helper, not a fully reliable travel agent.

Where are Indian travelers looking? According to Skift, interest is growing in cities such as Bishkek, Baku and Tashkent, as well as in Japan and Vietnam. When airline and hotel companies examine these numbers, they get useful insight. For tourism in Vietnam, this is remarkable news, because more Indians now plan trips overseas.
